At present her symptoms have stabilized on high doses of muscle relaxants and intermittent plasmaphoresis.

Over the course of her illness her valium requirements have increased and she now is on over 300 mg/d. An attempt to give a course of intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) was terminated because of aseptic meningitis. She has refused further IVIG treatment. More recently she has received 3 courses of treatment with plasmapheresis. These have produced a modest degree of improvement. The improvement, however, has lasted only several months. At present her symptoms have stabilized on high doses of muscle relaxants and intermittent plasmaphoresis. She continues to use a wheelchair though her muscle strength and coordination are actually sufficient for ambulation. During some of the spasms urinary stress incontinence occurs. Also, during some spasms her respiratory muscles lock in expiration and she becomes briefly apneic. She continues with psychotherapy for her PTSD. Overall her problems, though distressing, have become manageable.
